questions: Do the codex-cluster figures hold on re-measurement in this session?
What does the canonical detector report versus the raw sum, and why?
What are the classifier's grouping key and capability-shortfall rule at source?
What does the classifier actually produce against the live log?
Does the codex disclosure have two owners?
Does the corpus already implement cross-session recurrence detection?

findings.claim: Cluster figures unchanged: 29 events, 29 distinct sessions, all qor-audit, all sev 2; 40% of backlog, 43% of raw severity.
Those shares do not describe the gate. check_shadow_threshold sums via collapsed_severity: raw 134 -> collapsed 47. The codex cluster contributes 2 of 47.
Cross-session collapse already exists: _signature keys on (event_type, gate|capability|pattern), session absent by construction.
No dominant class: 47 spreads across 29 signatures, max contribution 3.
Classifier gap confirmed: 59 groups, 10 classifications, 18 events classified, 29 codex groups of size 1, 0 codex classified.
Last session's pending flip bought no discount: _pending_discount_applies needs closure_enforcer on the event; mark_addressed_pending does not propagate it.
evidence: measured: closure_enforcer is None on a flipped event

findings.claim: The disclosure has two owners: qor-audit Step 1.a and the environment adapter probe the same capability. Real as log-volume hygiene, not as a threshold finding.
